title: Cube-Root Limits for Clipped Quantile Effects on the Treated under Quadratic Overlap Failure
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field); paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4, and not salvageable within scope. Fresh math and decision panels pass with zero findings.
gap_reasons: The note proves a procedure-specific joint limit, smaller-sample bootstrap transfer, covariance factorization, and a conservative post-selection interval only for an exact quadratic propensity, uniform scalar covariate, and fixed public grid.
It does not prove that the n^{-1/3} rate is minimax or even competitive with estimators that exploit the imposed x-Lipschitz outcome structure, so the result is not a QTT rate frontier.
The variance ranking is already determined by the public grid, while the unresolved tied-selector behavior is bypassed by maximum calibration, limiting the substantive value of data-driven selection.

The framing is faithful about these restrictions, but the narrow constructed benchmark, absence of an optimality result, and lack of evidence that the procedure improves practically relevant inference keep the package below a field-level contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a uniform joint n^(1/3) law, refitted smaller-sample resampling with moment transfer, public-grid covariance, and a maximum-calibrated interval for the exact-quadratic QTT model. After a bounded cleanup of the first math-panel findings, fresh math and decision reviews passed with zero findings; D0.5.G nevertheless graded the contribution incremental because the fixed-grid procedure has no minimax or competitive-rate result and its variance ranking is public-grid determined. A broader positive result, an optimality converse, or a demonstrated practical inference gain remains open; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: Quadratic failure of control overlap makes the specified clipped QTT estimator converge at rate \(n^{1/3}\) to a non-Gaussian law. A public clipping grid shares one rare-event process, and fitting the square-root clipping drift applies a noisy oblique projection to that process. The proved joint law, fully refitted with-replacement \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) resampling, and moment transfer yield a public-grid covariance characterization and a data-only maximum-calibrated \(90\%\) interval with expected length \(O(n^{-1/3})\), uniformly even at exact variance ties. An explicit oscillatory endpoint law shows that selector-adaptive second-order shortening is not available on the current Lipschitz-in-\(x\) class without stronger endpoint smoothness and relative-rate conditions.
gap: The closest QTT paper establishes fixed-clipping marginal laws and implements fitted bias correction and bootstrap variance selection, but it does not establish the joint corrected law, full conditional resampling validity, covariance ranking, or coverage after selection.
fill: The four linked theorems turn the motivating workflow into a single uniform random-law result with moment-valid refitting and a feasible tie-robust interval of maximal expected length \(O(n^{-1/3})\).
